sentences.text: Theiophytalia was a herbivorous iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in Colorado, USA, during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
This animal belongs to the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
The genus name Theiophytalia is derived from the Greek words for "divine" and "garden" or "garden of the gods".
The species name kerri honors James Hutchinson Kerr, the discoverer of the specimen.
The skull found in 1878 at Garden of the Gods park in Colorado Springs is the only known fossil of the genus Theiophytalia.
A partial ornithopod skull was discovered in 1878 by James Kerr at Garden of the Gods park in El Paso County, Colorado.
The fossil skull, cataloged as YPM 1887, was originally identified by O.C. Marsh in 1886 and later affirmed by Gilmore in 1909 as belonging to the species Camptosaurus amplus.
Microscopic analysis revealed the skull came from the Lytle Member of the Purgatoire Formation, confirming it was Early Cretaceous in age rather than from the Morrison Formation.
The original description classified Theiophytalia as an intermediate form in derivation between Camptosaurus and Iguanodon.
Cladistic analyses from 2010 and 2011 recovered Theiophytalia as a basal member of Styracosterna, with Hippodraco identified as its closest relative.
Theiophytalia belongs to the parent group Styracosterna.
Theiophytalia lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Aptian to Albian stages.
